question: A shopkeeper sells an item at ₹68 and incurs a loss of 15%. At what price should he sell it to gain 20%?
solution:
**Given: **

At 68 he incurs a loss of 15%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** ⇒ (100 - 15)% = 68

 ⇒ 85% = 68

 ⇒ 1% = 68/85

 ∴ 20% gain = (100 + 20) % = (68/85) × 120

 ⇒ 96

**∴ The price when 20% gain is 96.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__ **

**Given:**

Selling price (SP, at loss) = ₹68

Loss % = 15%

Required gain % = 20%

**Concept Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (100 × SP)/(100 - loss %)

New Selling Price (SP, at gain) = CP × (1 + gain/100%)

**Calculation:**

CP = (100 × 68)/(100 - 15) = ₹80

⇒ New SP = 80 × (1 + 20/100) = ₹96

**∴ To gain 20%, the shopkeeper should sell the item at ₹96 **
